title: Neoliberal turn (Thatcher, Reagan, Washington Consensus)
summary: Neoliberal ideas, kept on the margins by Keynesian economics for decades, gained ground when stagflation struck in the 1970s. After Chile's early turn and the elections of Margaret Thatcher in Britain in 1979 and Ronald Reagan in the United States, they won wide influence on policy: more competition through deregulation and open markets, including for capital, and a smaller state through privatisation and limits on deficits. In 1990 John Williamson summed up the reforms urged on indebted Latin America as the Washington consensus.

uncertainty.note: Spans Margaret Thatcher taking office in May 1979 to John Williamson's codification of the Washington Consensus in late 1989.
